solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flat-finding agency

parts.note: reads like an estate agent hunting apartments, but describes a builder's tool that shows when a surface is truly horizontal

explanation.surface: An estate agency that specialises in finding apartments for clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is a British word for an apartment, which is the misleading sense; here it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubble tool is the instrument, or agency, by which a builder finds whether a surface is level.

clue.text: All he makes goes on horses

definitions.text: All he makes goes on horses

parts.words: All he makes goes on horses
parts.note: sounds like a gambler losing his wages at the races, but describes a craftsman whose leather goods are fitted to horses

explanation.surface: A man who spends every penny he earns betting on horse races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on horses' suggests betting; it really means his products are placed on horses' backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A leatherworker who makes seats and harness for riding is someone whose whole output is put on horses.

clue.text: Used in transporting other metals besides gold

definitions.text: Used in transporting other metals besides gold

indicators.note: the answer is used within, that is contained in, the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A remark about how precious metals are moved around.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold and other metals are cast into bars of standard shape for storage and transport.

clue.text: Crude, but in a gentle fashion

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or rework, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is rough in manner yet goes about it gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is the anagram signal; 'in a gentle fashion' reads as 'gently', but IN is taken literally and 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude manners are clumsy and lacking in grace or refinement, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Family row

definitions.meaning: a lineage, a family's descent
a ... is also a row, as in a ... of chairs

explanation.definitionFit: A lineage is a family's descent, and a straight series of things side by side is also so called.

clue.text: Scoundrels who show no compunction in breaking into houses

indicators.note: one piece breaks into, sits inside, the other

parts.note: villas are houses
taken as written

explanation.surface: Burglars who feel no guilt about breaking into people's homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Villains are wicked people, scoundrels who act without remorse or scruple.

clue.text: Being agile, he put the light on first

indicators.note: says the light piece comes first, before the word he

parts.note: with the light on, a room is lit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nimble man who switched on the light before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts LIT ahead of HE, though 'he' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and agile are near synonyms describing a body that bends and moves easily.

clue.text: Many set free

indicators.note: letters set free are loosened from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of prisoners released at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon releases many prisoners at once, so the whole clue defines it.

clue.text: The area isn't developed as well

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, describing a kind of well; the clue calls it the well

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the district has not been built up either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like 'as well' meaning 'too'; it is the definition, with 'The' and 'as' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore whose water rises under natural pressure is named after Artois, so the word stands for that kind of well.

clue.text: In which a boxer may drop his guard?

definitions.text: In which a boxer may drop his guard?

parts.words: In which a boxer may drop his guard?
parts.note: reads as a prizefighter in the ring, but the boxer is a breed of dog relaxing in its shelter

explanation.surface: A boxer letting his defences slip during a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer here is the dog breed, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's outdoor shelter is a place where a pet, perhaps a boxer, can rest off duty.

clue.text: I go round an Italian city

indicators.note: the second piece is placed round the first, enclosing it

parts.note: a go or turn is one's chance to play
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller describing a tour of an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts TURN around I; 'go' is a noun, as in 'your go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city in Piedmont, northern Italy.

clue.text: Refuse a stretcher

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun is rubbish dropped about
a stretcher or bed for carrying the sick

explanation.surface: Someone declining to use a stretcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered rubbish is called this, and so is a portable couch for carrying the wounded.

clue.text: Having no worries about being negligent

definitions.meaning: read as ..., without cares
not paying proper attention

explanation.surface: Someone untroubled by the charge of being sloppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the word means free of cares; in normal use it means negligent or sloppy.

clue.text: When students may collect on the streets

definitions.text: When students may collect on the streets

parts.words: When students may collect on the streets
parts.note: sounds like students gathering outdoors, but collect means raising money for charity

explanation.surface: Students gathering in town on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a British student charity event, with collections in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: British students hold an annual charity fundraising event with street collections and stunts.

clue.text: Girls get involved with men — trouble-makers

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled up and reordered

explanation.surface: Girls getting mixed up with men cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved' rearranges GIRLS and MEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gremlins are imaginary mischievous creatures blamed for mechanical faults, hence trouble-makers.

clue.text: The point in folly that becomes madness

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: folly is silliness, inanity
S is a point of the compass, south

explanation.surface: A philosophical observation that foolishness can tip over into lunacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S, a compass point, inside INANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanity and madness are synonyms for a deranged mind.

clue.text: Profit that shouldn't be taken unfairly

definitions.meaning: a benefit or gain
one should not take unfair ... of someone

explanation.surface: A moral warning about gains made at others' expense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a benefit or gain, and the idiom 'take unfair advantage' supplies the second sense.

clue.text: Gilbert's partner seen in foreign villa in blazer

indicators.note: the jumbled piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the sun blazes, so it is a blazer

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a blazer spotted at a villa abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' turns VILLA into LLIVA, which goes 'in' SUN. Arthur Sullivan wrote the music for W S Gilbert's comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Composer Arthur Sullivan partnered librettist W S Gilbert in the Savoy operas.

clue.text: An old story that bears fruit

definitions.meaning: a stale, much-repeated joke or tale
a tree that produces edible nuts

explanation.surface: A tale about something fruitful.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed tale is so called, and the same name belongs to a tree yielding edible nuts.

clue.text: Order the ambitious officer hopes to get

definitions.meaning: an instruction

definitions.text: the ambitious officer hopes to get
definitions.meaning: an officer wants charge of a unit or ship

explanation.surface: An ambitious officer hopes for a particular instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an instruction, and also authority over troops or a ship, which officers seek.

clue.text: Drive to a meeting place?

parts.note: a venue is where people meet

explanation.surface: Driving to a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' is a noun, a road, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and avenue are both names for a road, often tree-lined.

clue.text: Not slow to voice an opinion

definitions.meaning: fast, like a fast train
to state or put into words

explanation.surface: Someone quick to speak their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fast, as of a train, and also to put a view into words.

clue.text: Spot a complicated clue — but it's of little matter

parts.note: a mole is a spot on the skin

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver notices a tricky clue but decides it doesn't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' is the anagram signal on 'clue'; the definition puns on 'of little matter' as 'a tiny piece of matter' rather than 'unimportant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is a tiny particle of matter, read here as 'of little matter'.

clue.text: Organ stop

definitions.meaning: part of the large intestine, a body organ
a punctuation mark

explanation.surface: A stop on a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: It names part of the gut, a bodily organ, and also a punctuation mark, a kind of stop.

clue.text: Catch in Antwerp on the loose without wife

indicators.note: letters on the loose run free and are rearranged
without means the letter is removed

explanation.surface: Trying to capture a fugitive in Antwerp after his wife left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes W from ANTWERP, leaving ANTERP, which 'on the loose' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare or trap someone is to catch them.

clue.text: Bring up a matter of higher wages

definitions.meaning: to rear a child, or to mention
a pay rise

explanation.surface: Mentioning the subject of a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to rear or mention, and in American usage the noun is a pay increase.

clue.text: Summons author without hesitation

indicators.note: without means those letters are taken away

parts.note: an author is a writer
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A writer is called to court without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a legal document, such as a summons to appear in court.

clue.text: Article left out of yearbook creates void

indicators.note: the article is left out, removed from the longer word

parts.note: an annual is a yearly book
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Missing a piece makes a yearbook incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' removes A from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a contract or marriage is to declare it void, so it creates nullity.

clue.text: Poor relatives prepared to do a variety of jobs

definitions.text: prepared to do a variety of jobs

indicators.note: poor in the sense of badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Impoverished family members willing to take any work.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptable people able to turn their hand to many tasks are described with this word.

clue.text: In spite of it, all the more

definitions.meaning: however, despite that
taken literally, not at all less

explanation.surface: Despite everything, even more so.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means however or despite that; read literally as not less, it means all the more.
